outputs.label: Energy the house uses a day
Units the system makes a month

answer: A typical 5 marla house with fans, LED lights, an inverter fridge, a TV, one 1.5 ton inverter AC, a water pump and an iron needs a solar system of about {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW ({{out.panels|int}} panels of {{out.panel_w|int}} W) with a {{out.inverter_kw|up2}} kW inverter. The panels are sized from the daily units ÷ the city's sun yield; the grid covers the moments when everything runs at once.
how: Energy: each appliance's watts × quantity × hours a day (an inverter AC counts at its average draw, below its rated watts), added up = {{out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day; ÷ {{out.yield_kwh_per_kwp_day|1}} units per kW of panels a day for your city = {{out.kw_energy|2}} kW. A grid-tied or hybrid system is sized by energy: when the {{out.running_w|int}} W running load is more than the panels give at that moment, the grid supplies the rest. {{out.kw|2}} kW needs {{out.panels|int}} panels of {{out.panel_w}} W = {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW installed, which makes about {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month. Inverter: the larger of {{out.running_w|int}} W × {{out.margin|2}} = {{out.inverter_kw_load|2}} kW for the load and {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels ÷ {{out.dc_ac_ratio_max|1}} = {{out.inverter_kw_array|2}} kW, so the panels are never more than {{out.dc_ac_ratio_max|1}} times the inverter: {{out.inverter_kw|up2}} kW continuous, with a surge rating of at least {{out.inverter_surge_w|int}} W for the water pump.
key_facts: A typical 5 marla house with one 1.5 ton inverter AC has a running load of about {{out.running_w|int}} W and uses about {{out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day, so it needs a solar system of about {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW with a {{out.inverter_kw|up2}} kW inverter.
Solar system size in kW = units a day ÷ sun yield per kW a day. With the grid connected the panels do not have to carry every appliance at once; only an off-grid system is sized that way.
One kW of panels makes about {{out.yield_kwh_per_kwp_day|1}} units a day in Lahore over the year, so a {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW system makes about {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month.
Panels are counted up to the next whole panel: {{out.kw|2}} kW ÷ {{out.panel_w|int}} W = {{out.panels|int}} panels, about {{out.roof_m2|int}} square metres of roof.

formula.text: kW = E_day ÷ yield (grid-tied or hybrid; P_run ÷ 1000 ÷ PR is the off-grid rule, shown for comparison); panels = ceil(kW × 1000 ÷ W_panel)
lines: E_day = Σ (watts × qty × hours) ÷ 1000, units used a day
yield = units one kW of panels makes a day in your city
P_run = total running watts, PR = performance ratio
Inverter W = max(P_run × margin, kW × 1000 ÷ r_max), r_max = largest panel-to-inverter (DC/AC) ratio; surge ≥ largest starting load
Battery Ah = P_run × night hours ÷ (V × DoD × η)

sections.h2: What is the electrical load of a 5 marla house?
p: A 5 marla house usually has two or three bedrooms, a lounge, a kitchen and one or two bathrooms. The default list above is what runs in such a house in summer: four ceiling fans, ten LED bulbs, an inverter fridge, a TV, one 1.5 ton inverter AC, a water pump and an iron. Together they come to {{out.running_w|int}} W running and {{out.daily_kwh|1}} units a day, which is about {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month from the solar system.

The daily units, not the running load, set the panel size here. The AC, the pump and the fans can all be on at noon, and when their {{out.running_w|int}} W is more than the panels give, the grid supplies the rest. The running load still sets the inverter. If your house has fewer or more appliances, change the list and the result updates.

sections.h2: How many kW solar for a 5 marla house?
p: For the typical house above the answer is {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels with a {{out.inverter_kw|up2}} kW inverter. The energy rule asks for {{out.kw_energy|2}} kW. Panels big enough to carry the whole {{out.running_w|int}} W at midday ({{out.running_w|int}} W ÷ {{out.pr|2}} = {{out.kw_power|2}} kW) would make more units than the house uses, and the extra would be sold at the low buyback rate; that rule is for off-grid systems, which have no grid to fall back on.
The panel count is rounded up, so the installed size is a little above the calculated {{out.kw|2}} kW. Installers quote by inverter size, which is why this house is sold as a five kW system.

sections.h2: When is a 5 kW solar system right for a 5 marla house?
p: A five kW inverter with {{out.panels|int}} panels suits a 5 marla house with one inverter AC, fans, lights, a fridge and a pump, which is exactly the default above. It runs the whole house in the day and feeds spare units to the grid.
With two inverter ACs running at the same time the running load goes above the inverter rating, and the calculator moves you to the next size. See the second worked example below for that house.

sections.h2: Solar for a 5 marla house with one AC
p: One 1.5 ton inverter AC is the single biggest load in the list. On average it draws about {{d.ac_inverter_avg_kw_1_5_ton|1}} kW while running, which is most of the house's daily units in summer. The default result is the one-AC case: {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels and a {{out.inverter_kw|up2}} kW inverter.
If the AC is non-inverter, the starting surge is much larger and the inverter must handle it. Pick the non-inverter AC in the list and the surge rating in the result changes.

sections.h2: What does a 5 marla solar system cost?
p: We do not print a price here because panel and inverter prices in Pakistan move with the dollar rate and change from month to month. Ask for quotes in Rs per watt of panels, so a {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW system is compared like for like; a quote checker that compares your quote against the current market range is coming to this site.

A complete quote must include the panels, the inverter, the mounting structure, DC and AC cables, breakers and surge protection, earthing, installation labour and, for a grid-tied system, the net-metering or net-billing application and the bidirectional meter. A quote that leaves any of these out looks cheaper than it is.

sections.h2: Do you need a battery for a 5 marla solar system?
p: A grid-tied system with no battery is the cheapest and runs the house in the day; at night you buy from the grid. If your area has load shedding after sunset, enter the hours of backup you want and the calculator adds a lithium battery sized for the full running load for those hours.

The battery figure is for every appliance in your list running after dark. Most houses run only fans, lights and the fridge at night, so make a second list without the AC and pump to size a smaller battery.

mistakes: Sizing the panels to run every appliance at once. That is the off-grid rule; with the grid connected it buys panels whose extra units are sold back at the low buyback rate.
Forgetting the pump and iron. They run for minutes, but they are on the running load when they do, and the pump's starting surge sets the inverter's surge rating.

Buying an inverter equal to the panel kW without checking the load. The inverter is sized from the running load with a margin, and only raised when the panels would be more than {{d.dc_ac_ratio_max|1}} times it; the panels are sized from the daily units, so the two numbers usually differ.

Expecting the rated panel watts every day. The performance ratio of {{d.pr|pct}} covers heat, dust, cable loss and cloudy days; the units a month shown is the realistic yearly average, not a sunny-day peak.
Sizing a battery for the whole house. The battery line assumes every listed appliance runs after dark; list only the night loads for a battery you can afford.
safety: A rooftop solar system connects to the grid and to your house wiring at mains voltage; have a licensed electrician and a DISCO-approved installer do the wiring, earthing and net-metering connection.

faq.q: How many solar panels does a 5 marla house need?
faq.a: The typical 5 marla house above needs {{out.panels|int}} panels of {{out.panel_w|int}} W, which is {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW and about {{out.roof_m2|int}} square metres of roof. Smaller panels mean more panels for the same kW.

faq.q: Is a 5 kW solar system enough for a 5 marla house?
faq.a: Yes for one 1.5 ton inverter AC with fans, lights, a fridge and a pump, which needs {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW of panels and a {{out.inverter_kw|up2}} kW inverter. For two ACs at the same time, or an electric geyser, the calculator moves to the next size.

faq.q: How many units will a 5 marla solar system make a month?
faq.a: About {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month for the {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW system in Lahore, as a yearly average. Summer months make more and winter months less; choose your city above for its own sun yield.

faq.q: Can I run a 1.5 ton AC on a 5 marla solar system?
faq.a: Yes. The panels make the house's daily units, the AC's included, and when the AC and the rest together draw more than the panels give at that moment, the grid supplies the difference. In the evening the AC runs from the grid or from a battery.

faq.q: What is the price of a solar system for a 5 marla house?
faq.a: Prices change with the dollar rate, so we do not print one. Compare quotes in Rs per watt for a complete system of {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW, including structure, cables, protection, installation and the net-metering application.

faq.q: Grid-tied, hybrid or off-grid for a 5 marla house?
faq.a: Grid-tied is cheapest and sells spare units to the grid. Hybrid adds a battery for load shedding, sized with the backup hours field above. Off-grid needs a battery for every night and cloudy day and is rarely worth it where the grid is available.

faq.q: Why does the result change when I add an appliance that runs for a few minutes?
faq.a: The panels follow the daily units, so a short-running appliance adds only its few units. It still counts in the running load, which sets the inverter, and a pump's start sets the inverter's surge rating.
